text:
sam: Heads up — onboarding CI for the new sampleapp keeps failing in the typegen step after the auth/retry changes landed. Seen this a few times today.

tara: ugh, seen it once too. looks like regendiff is non-deterministic? sometimes the generated types reorder optional params.

jen: can you paste the CI snippet?

sam: here — failing job output: ```
Run yarn typegen
> regenerating types...
diff --git a/src/types.ts b/src/types.ts
@@ -10,6 +10,6 @@ export type CreateUser = {
-  email?: string | null;
+  email: string;
   name?: string;
```
The CI claims a breaking change even though codegen inputs didn't change (only auth/retry behavior tweak merged).

mike: that looks like a semver vs shape issue. typegen picks up `required` differently when operation has 2 examples in openapi. Might be nondet sorting in the OpenAPI file.

sam: I ran `openapi-generator-cli generate` locally and got the same flip when running twice in a row. So it's nondet. Not caused by the auth patch directly, but the auth/retry change added a tiny comment block in the sampleapp's openapi.yaml (whitespace + example ordering) which seems to surface the nondeterminism.

dx-bot: buildbot: rerun job #3521 requested by sam

buildbot: rerun started — job 3521 (typegen)

tara: short-term: we can tweak the CI to run `yarn typegen && git diff --exit-code || (yarn typegen --regen && git add -A && git commit -m "chore: sync typegen" && echo "regen committed")` but that hides the root cause.

jen: long term we should make the typegen output deterministic or canonicalize the openapi before generation (sort object keys, stable examples order). Also add a checkbox in the release checklist: "run sampleapp regen twice to catch nondet flips".

mike: idea: add a small step that normalizes `x-examples` ordering and strips comment-only whitespace changes before feed into generator. Cheap and effective.

sam: agree. For immediate unblock, I pushed a temp patch to sampleapp that pins the generated types in a fenced commit and skipped the commit check in CI. Patch: `ci: temporarily relax typegen strictness for onboarding` — it's in PR #412.

tara: can you also add a note in the PR body about semver risk? I don't want an accidental major bump from a nondet reordering.

sam: done. PR body includes: "No API surface change intended. This is a deterministic-output workaround while we implement canonicalization. See follow-up issue: #2330"

jen: filing issue now: `devex#2330` "stabilize typegen/OpenAPI canonicalization — prevent regen diffs from whitespace/order nondeterminism". assigning to eng-ml and devex.

mike: FYI this also impacts SDK parity checks — if typegen flips optional vs required between runs, our semver gate thinks we've introduced a breaking change and blocks publishing. That explains the earlier publish flake.

sam: exact. The publish gate currently treats any type change as a major-ish signal. We should only treat user-visible contract changes as semver-major candidates.

tara: agreed. we should update the publish tooling to run a shallow structural comparison that ignores ordering-only diffs and comment/description-only edits.

jen: for the immediate release cutoff, maintainers: if you see a regen-only change that is all reorder/description only, feel free to mark `release: allow` in the PR and note the CI flake reference. But file the canonicalization issue.

sam: one more note — auth/retry test flakiness popped up in a different CI job when the sampleapp's mocked responses changed ordering. Might be related. I'll add a deterministic seed to the mock server to avoid brittle tests.

mike: sounds good. I'll pick up the canonicalizer tomorrow and prototype a small Node script that loads openapi, sorts keys, normalizes example arrays, and writes a stable YAML.

tara: thanks — big win for onboarding friction if we remove these false-positive blocks. :+1:

jen: tagging infra for potential CI change: @mike @tara — could use a lightweight gating change for the next 48h to unstick a couple onboarding PRs.

buildbot: build #3521 succeeded on rerun

sam: thanks all, reran onboarding queue and things are unstuck. follow-up work tracked in devex#2330 and sampleapp PR #412.

jen: closing loop — will add a blurb to the docs about typegen determinism and the interim workaround for maintainers.
